records.unitTitle: How do assessment reviews and appeals work?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: An assessment challenge begins with a request for review to the Director; the Act then provides the appeal route to the Assessment and Planning Appeal Board and a further court route on questions of law.

records.unitTitle: Watercourse and wetland alterations: when are plans and permits required?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Before undertaking a qualifying project or structure that alters a watercourse or wetland or diverts water, the person must provide the Minister with the required plans/information and, unless exempted or waived under the Act, obtain the required permit.

records.unitTitle: What is a condominium property and what does registration create?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Registration of the declaration and description brings the described land and appurtenant interests under the Condominium Property Act and creates the condominium corporation whose members are the owners.

records.unitTitle: What survey material must a condominium description contain?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.

records.unitTitle: What is a conservation easement and how is it created, registered, changed and enforced?

registration gives it effect;
the Act governs amendment, assignment, termination and enforcement.

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: For a general way/easement/water-use claim, 20 years of qualifying enjoyment receives statutory protection against the specified historical-origin objection, while 40 years can make the right absolute and indefeasible unless the statutory written-consent exception applies.

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.

records.unitTitle: How are highway location, width, boundaries, discontinuance and access controlled?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Where doubt or dispute arises as to the boundaries of a highway, the Highway Act deems a line along the centre line of the travelled portion to be the centre line of the highway.

records.unitTitle: Recovery of land, dispossession and expiry of title

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.

records.unitTitle: Recovery of land, dispossession and expiry of title

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.

records.unitTitle: How are mineral claims located and what land rights follow a claim?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: A mineral claim is described using the New Brunswick Mineral and Petroleum Grid and referenced to UTM grid coordinates in NAD83(CSRS), and the claim-area boundaries extend vertically downward.

records.unitTitle: Boundary surveys under the Mining Act

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: A boundary survey under the Mining Act must be carried out by a land surveyor qualified under New Brunswick law and in accordance with the Surveys Act.

records.unitTitle: Boundary surveys under the Mining Act

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Angles in such a boundary survey are designated by coordinates under the Surveys Act coordinate system, and orthometric heights use CGVD2013 based on a benchmark approved by the Director of Surveys.

coreUnderstanding: Minister may order the survey;
surveyor has statutory entry rights for the survey subject to avoiding unnecessary damage;

records.unitTitle: Entry onto private land and the survey framework for oil and gas rights

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Where the holder cannot obtain the necessary agreement with the owner, tenant or occupant of private land, the Act provides a statutory special-order process for entry and use rather than an unrestricted right of entry.

records.unitTitle: Which conveyancing and easement rules in the Property Act matter to surveyors?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Subject to a contrary intention in the conveyance, a conveyance of land can carry the appurtenant ways, waters, watercourses, easements, rights and other interests described by the Act.

records.unitTitle: Entry, surveying, designation and compensation for public works

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: For purposes connected with a public work, the Act authorizes the Minister and the authorized architects, engineers, agents and workers to enter land, survey and take levels, and make the specified investigative borings or trial pits.

records.unitTitle: Surveyed lease areas, changes, reclamation and filing

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: A quarry lease over Crown Lands requires the boundaries of the Crown Lands to be covered by the lease to have been surveyed in accordance with the regulations.

records.unitTitle: When does Real Property Transfer Tax apply to a land transfer?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: The Act imposes transfer tax in connection with registration of a deed, using the statutory comparison between consideration and assessed value.

records.unitTitle: How does the Trespass Act interact with statutory authority to enter land?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: The Trespass Act does not apply to a person who enters or remains on premises under authority of an Act of the New Brunswick Legislature or an Act of the Parliament of Canada.

records.unitTitle: Registry or Land Titles: which registration system am I in?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Before applying registration rules, determine whether the parcel is governed by Registry or Land Titles; the two systems give registration different legal effects.

unitContext.examGoal: Given a land-registration fact pattern, first identify whether the parcel is governed by Registry or Land Titles and route the issue into the correct registration system.
coreUnderstanding: Registry and Land Titles are different land-registration systems and registration has different legal consequences under each.
The first routing question in many title/registration problems is therefore which system governs the parcel.
Registry problems generally direct the candidate toward instruments, registration, execution, plans and priority.
Land Titles problems generally direct the candidate toward registered ownership, registered interests, parcel changes, rectification and indemnification.

lookupContext.prompt: Registry — legal effect of a registered conveyance

records.unitTitle: Solving a boundary problem: where do I look first, and when do I escalate?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: A surveyor's boundary investigation/determination and a statutory confirmation of a boundary under the Boundaries Confirmation Act are different processes.

unitContext.examGoal: Route a boundary uncertainty or dispute through title records, survey evidence, special statutory boundary rules and, when necessary, the formal Boundaries Confirmation process.
coreUnderstanding: Boundary work begins with title/record research and field/survey evidence, not automatically with a statutory confirmation proceeding.
Special statutes can modify the analysis for particular boundaries, including Crown land and highways.

The Boundaries Confirmation Act supplies a formal statutory process for resolving/confirming a disputed or uncertain boundary; it is not the same thing as the surveyor performing the underlying boundary investigation.

records.unitTitle: Easements, rights-of-way and other interests: what kind of right is this?

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Do not apply the Easements Act prescriptive periods mechanically to registered Land Titles land; check the Land Titles Act rules governing prescription and pre-registration rights.

unitContext.examGoal: Classify an easement/right-of-way fact pattern by how the interest arose and route it through prescription, express grants, Land Titles, conservation or Crown-land legislation as applicable.
coreUnderstanding: First identify how the claimed right arose.
Prescription, an express written grant, a conservation easement, a Crown-land easement and a registered Land Titles interest are not interchangeable legal routes.
Land Titles status can materially change the prescription analysis.

lookupContext.prompt: Land Titles effect on unregistered/prescriptive interests

records.unitTitle: Government entry, use and acquisition of private land

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: A statutory right to enter land to survey, inspect or investigate is not the same thing as expropriating the land or acquiring title to it.

unitContext.examGoal: Distinguish statutory authority to enter land for surveying or investigation from statutory acquisition/expropriation of an interest in the land.
coreUnderstanding: A right to enter land for surveying, inspection, testing or investigation does not itself necessarily transfer ownership.
Different statutes supply different entry powers for different purposes.
Where title or possession is actually being taken, follow the relevant acquisition/expropriation and compensation framework.

records.unitTitle: Condominiums and three-dimensional parcels

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: An air-space parcel and a condominium unit are not interchangeable concepts; they are created and governed through different statutory schemes.

unitContext.examGoal: Distinguish air-space parcels from condominium property and route three-dimensional parcel and condominium survey questions into the correct statutory regime.
coreUnderstanding: Air-space parcels and condominium units are different statutory concepts.
An Air Space Act plan creates and defines an air-space parcel using the Act's three-dimensional plan requirements.
The Condominium Property Act governs declarations/descriptions, units, common elements and bare-land condominium survey requirements.
Registration requirements remain relevant after the specialized plan requirements are satisfied.

records.unitTitle: Evidence, records and historical title research

currentCard.currentPrompt: State the key rule you should remember for this curriculum unit.
currentCard.currentExpectedAnswer: Finding or obtaining a record and proving or using that record as evidence are separate questions: land-registration and archival statutes govern records/access, while the Evidence Act supplies evidentiary routes for qualifying records and copies.

unitContext.examGoal: Route a historical title or boundary-research problem through current land-registration records, archival/public records and the separate evidentiary rules governing how records may be proved or used.
coreUnderstanding: Finding/accessing a record and proving/using that record as evidence are different legal questions.
Registry, Land Titles, Archives and Public Records provisions help locate, preserve or access records.
The Evidence Act supplies routes by which qualifying records, certified copies, maps, plans and survey records can be received as evidence.
Formal boundary-confirmation work has its own evidence/application requirements.
